TYPICAL PEDON.content:
TYPICAL PEDON: Collier ashy sandy loam, forested, on a 3 percent slope at an elevation of 1760 meters. (Colors are for dry soil unless otherwise noted.)
Oi--0 to 3 centimeters; slightly decomposed plant material
A--3 to 13 centimeters; ashy sandy loam; dark yellowish brown (10YR 4/4), very dark brown (10YR 2/2), moist; 4 percent field estimated clay; weak fine granular structure; very friable, nonsticky, nonplastic; many very fine and fine roots and common medium roots throughout; many fine low-continuity interstitial pores; 3 percent subangular andesite gravel, 5 percent subrounded pumice paragravel; slightly acid (pH 6.1); clear wavy boundary
BA--13 to 30 centimeters; ashy loamy sand; brown (7.5YR 5/2), dark brown (7.5YR 3/2), moist; 3 percent field estimated clay; weak fine subangular blocky structure; very friable, nonsticky, nonplastic; many very fine and fine roots throughout; many fine low-continuity interstitial pores; 3 percent subangular andesite gravel, 5 percent subrounded pumice paragravel; slightly acid (pH 6.1); clear wavy boundary
Bw--30 to 58 centimeters; ashy paragravelly loamy sand; light brown (7.5YR 6/3), brown (7.5YR 4/2), moist; 3 percent field estimated clay; weak fine subangular blocky structure; very friable, nonsticky, nonplastic; few very fine roots throughout; many fine low-continuity interstitial pores; 8 percent subrounded andesite gravel, 15 percent subrounded pumice paragravel; slightly acid (pH 6.1); clear wavy boundary
C--58 to 157 centimeters; paragravelly ashy sand; light brown (7.5YR 6/4), brown (7.5YR 4/4), moist; single grain; loose; nonsticky, nonplastic; few fine roots throughout; many fine low-continuity interstitial pores; 8 percent subrounded andesite gravel, 15 percent subrounded pumice paragravel; neutral (pH 6.6)
